cards.text: Psalm 150 is the very last psalm, and it opens with a shout: "Hallelujah! Praise God in His sanctuary." No warm-up, friend. The oven's already HOT.

cards.question: In Psalm 150, the call to praise God stays inside His sanctuary and goes nowhere else.

cards.text: Nope, it climbs: "Praise Him in His mighty heavens." That's not one room, friend. That's the room, the roof and EVERYTHING above the roof.

cards.question: Psalm 150 also says what to praise God for. One reason is His mighty acts. What's the other one?

cards.text: Then the psalm calls in the band: "Praise Him with the sound of the horn; praise Him with the harp and lyre." Me, I've got one instrument, the oven timer, and it knows exactly ONE song. DING.

cards.question: Along with the tambourine, Psalm 150 calls for praising God with dancing.

cards.text: Tambourine AND dancing, then strings and flute. You ever seen a stamper dance on a gold base, friend? It's hopping. Very dignified hopping.

cards.question: In verse 5, the last instruments Psalm 150 names, it calls for praising God with ___ two times in a row.

cards.text: "Praise Him with clashing cymbals; praise Him with resounding cymbals." Years in that junk drawer, the loudest thing I ever heard was a dead battery rolling over, and now the psalm wants CYMBALS. TWO KINDS.

cards.question: Psalm 150 has called in the whole band. Then it turns to who should praise the LORD. Who does it call?

cards.text: "Let everything that has breath praise the LORD!" Friend, I'm a stamper on a gold base with no lungs at ALL, and you better believe I'm still waving this mustache.

cards.question: Psalm 150 ends with the same word it starts with.

findings.problem: The opening card doesn't say who is speaking or who is being addressed. It never mentions the psalmist or the call going out to the listener. It only says the psalm opens with a shout.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: "Nope, it climbs" and "That's not one room... That's the room, the roof and EVERYTHING above the roof" treat the sanctuary as an earthly room under a roof and the heavens as a step up from it. The text doesn't say what the sanctuary is or how it connects to the heavens.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The card asks the baker to guess the wording of the second half of verse 2 ("His excellent greatness" against "His tender mercy" and "His holy name"). No story card sets up verse 2, so nothing lets the baker reason it out. It is a pure wording guess.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: No story card sets up verse 4. Card 5 ends on verse 3 and the oven timer joke. Whether "dancing" goes with the tambourine is a wording guess with no context to reason from.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: "In verse 5, the last instruments Psalm 150 names..." points to a verse number like a test question. It doesn't read as Papa Dorin pausing mid-passage.

rule.text: Ask from inside the passage, the way a storyteller pauses to let the listener lean in. The question comes out of the moment Papa Dorin just set up.

findings.problem: "CYMBALS. TWO KINDS." states as fact that clashing and resounding cymbals are two different kinds of cymbals. The text only gives the two descriptions and doesn't say whether they are different instruments.

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: The baker never sees the closing "Hallelujah!". Card 11 quotes verse 6 but stops before it. So whether the psalm ends with the same word it starts with is a guess at the last word of the final line.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.
